bibliography.abstract: This study develops a reproducible, data-driven optimisation framework for analysing national-scale routing efficiency within South Korea’s road-ferry transport network. Using empirically derived travel distances and durations obtained from the OpenRouteService (ORS) API, an 85 x 85 origin–destination matrix was constructed to represent nationwide road-ferry connectivity, including links to Jeju Island. Two maritime accessibility scenarios were evaluated: a multi-port configuration (Mokpo, Yeosu, Busan, and Incheon) and a restricted single-port configuration (Mokpo only). Multiple optimisation approaches, including constructive heuristics, local-search methods (2-opt, 3-opt, and Lin-Kernighan), Simulated Annealing, and the exact Concorde solver, were benchmarked to assess solution quality and performance. Results indicate that advanced optimisation methods achieved shorter tours, with Concorde and Lin-Kernighan both identifying the optimal solution. Scenario analysis reveals the importance of maritime accessibility for national routing efficiency. The multi-port configuration achieved approximately 17.2 % shorter travel distance and 8.4 % shorter travel duration than the single-port configuration, demonstrating the benefits of diversified ferry connectivity. Furthermore, distance-based and duration-based optimisation produced structurally distinct routing configurations despite similar aggregate efficiency, highlighting the sensitivity of network topology to objective function selection. Stability analysis showed that the 2-opt heuristic converged consistently to a narrow solution band (coefficient of variation < 2 % across 100 runs), supporting its suitability as a baseline method for comparative accessibility analysis. Methodologically, the study integrates open geospatial routing data with classical optimisation techniques within a transparent and scalable workflow. The resulting framework provides a reproducible benchmark for evaluating road-ferry accessibility and a foundation for future multimodal transport modelling and infrastructure planning.
